note: Clean pass with caveats. Source is the EANNA 2023 deposit itself (BIDAT dataset e3ceb7aa-95a8-4838-909b-155719847d21, licence 'Creative Commons Attribution'; Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia, fieldwork by INE). WORDS: the administered child questionnaire 'Cuestionario_Ninos_y_Ninas_5_a_8_anos_EANNA_2023.pdf' (sha256 309f6f782390064760f87c01b7a798fd258cb794dd0e9b3dc3f1801bd72573a0), read to the child face-to-face by an interviewer; every shipped Spanish string (41 item texts, 4 section prompts, the instructions) was checked as a whitespace-normalised substring of the PDF's own text layer, 0 misses, and read against the rendered pages. Its preface states 'Las alternativas de respuesta se encuentra numeradas y coinciden con el valor que aparece en la base de datos'. MAPPING: the codebook 'Libro de codigos base de datos EANNA 2023' (sha256 0478c51b7101a71a5a70f1219f1d17e4752f9cff1d0e50ab98118e02e547306a), sheet '3. NN', gives every variable NAME its label, value labels and frequencies. (1) Code derivation: the do-file's 'Ninos y Ninas 5 a 8 anos' block (nna_selec!=0, rp2!=1, ages 5-8) writes gen item = "`var'", so `item` IS the source Stata variable name (exempt pattern); mapping_basis=data_labels. Checked against the data anyway by route 9: all 88 codebook item x value cells for the 41 items (excluding -88/-99/-98, which the do-file decodes to missing) equal the live counts exactly (e.g. n5 46/595/4459, n6 992/2760/1320, n9 3594/1301/210, n10 40/4937/114/20/0, n7_4 1030/4092, n8_1 772/4377, n11_2 3440/1709, n15 380/4032, n16 772/4284). 40 of 41 profiles are distinct; n8_87 and n8_99 tie at 12 'Si' each but are disjoint sets of respondents (overlap 0), so they are different columns, and the tie is resolved only by the variable-name derivation, not by route 9. (2) Shape: n7_* and n8_* are multiple-select questions ('Registre todas las alternativas que correspondan') stored as one 0/1 dummy per alternative, including the non-substantive alternatives 78 'A nadie', 87 'No aplica', 88 'No sabe', 99 'No responde' (dummies n7_78..n7_99, n8_78..n8_99); the shared question is section_prompt, the alternative is item_text, option_text is the codebook's 0='No'/1='Si'. n11_* are separate Si/No questions shown with cards TH1-TH12; n11_1a/n11_1b are follow-ups asked only if n11_1=1. n10's section_prompt is the static text read before it ('Ahora vamos a conversar sobre las cosas...'), to which its 'estas cosas' refers; n11's section_prompt is the static text 'Ahora te voy a preguntar por las cosas de la casa que tu haces.' (its green highlighting not reproduced). instructions = the questionnaire's opening text read to the child ('Hola, mi nombre es %nombre encuestador%...'), which precedes both modules. n5, n6, n9, n15, n16 are single questions with blank section_prompt. (3) Stripped and disclosed: interviewer-facing blue text ('Lea alternativas', 'Registre todas las alternativas que correspondan', 'Espere respuesta espontanea y clasifique', the n10 probing instruction, 'Muestre tarjeta TH..', the multi-dwelling note), the '(NO LEER)' marker on alternatives 78 and 87 (shipped 'A nadie', 'No aplica'), skip arrows and 'Condicion habilitante' lines. Dynamic text is shipped as the study's own published placeholder: '%nombre encuestador%' in instructions and '%tareas del hogar 5 a 8%' in n15 (filled at interview time with the tasks the child reported in n11). (4) Questionnaire vs codebook wording: the questionnaire ships where they differ -- n5 codebook 'En general, ...' vs questionnaire '¿Como te va en el colegio o jardin?'; n9 codebook 'Actualmente, ...' vs 'Pensando en como te sientes actualmente, ...'; n7 codebook 'En el colegio o jardin, ¿a quien le pides ayuda?' vs 'Cuando tienes algun problema en el colegio o jardin, ...'; n8_4 codebook 'A un profesor' vs 'A un profesor(a)'; n11_3/n11_4/n11_8/n11_9/n11_10/n11_12 labels truncate the questionnaire's examples; n15/n16 labels drop the lead-in sentence. (5) Options: n10 has a fifth alternative '5. Un nino(a) o adolescente que no es de su familia (Por ejemplo, un vecino(a))' that no respondent chose (codebook frequency 0, absent from live resp); it is not shipped because the resp-set gate admits only observed values. -88 'No sabe'/-99 'No responde'/-98 'Sin Dato' are decoded to missing by the do-file and have no rows. Direction differs by item and is shipped as coded: n5 1=Mal..3=Bien (ascending), but n6 1=Mucho..3=Nada (fighting) and n9 1=Muy contento..3=Nada contento (descending). n10 and the n7/n8 dummies are nominal, not ordinal. (6) Skip structure (per-item n differ by design; checked on the live table): n5-n9 asked if attending school/kindergarten or on holiday/strike (5,122 of 5,149 ids; n7_* NA for exactly 27); n11_1a/n11_1b n=978 = n11_1 'Si' 980 minus 2 'Sin Dato'; n15 asked of the 4,454 ids with any n11_*=1 (4,412 answered + 27 -88 + 15 -99), 0 answers among ids with no task. (7) Language: administered orally in Spanish, which ships in the base fields. The deposit has no English version, so the _translated columns are IRW's own translation (translation_source=machine_translation); public_note written. (8) Rights: no clause reserving a right is locatable; grep of the questionnaire text for derech/licen/copyright/reproduc/prohib/autoriz/creative returns only survey content. The instrument is the Chilean state's own survey questionnaire, published in full by the agency alongside a CC BY dataset. No register row written. (9) Step 3b: the dictionary Description ('children aged 5-8, particularly their principal activities and relationships with others') matches the live items, which are the 5-8 child questionnaire's education/perception and household-tasks modules; n1-n4 and n14 are dropped by the do-file and n17+ (economic activities) are not in this table. (10) irw-validate (upload profile) passes with one WARN, name_charset (hyphens), a property of the pre-existing response table NAME (irw#2365; the name is 40 characters, within the cap); `table` must reproduce the live name for the join, so it was left as published.
public_note: The English in the _translated columns of this table was produced by IRW, not by the study: EANNA 2023 published its questionnaire only in Spanish, and the Spanish in the base fields is what the children (aged 5-8) heard from the interviewer. Response codes run in different directions across items (n5 1=Mal to 3=Bien, but n6 1=Mucho to 3=Nada and n9 1=Muy contento to 3=Nada contento), n10 is a nominal who-does-the-housework item, and n7_*/n8_* are 0/1 dummies of a multiple-select question that include non-substantive alternatives (A nadie, No aplica, No sabe, No responde)

note: Response data: Kaggle 'imo-scores' (kaggle.com/datasets/luckyt/imo-scores, CC0 per sibling imos_* checks). Item codes problem1..problem6 are the Kaggle file's own column names, kept verbatim by data/imos_2018.r (pivot_longer over starts_with('Problem')); no rename, no positional step. Item text: official English problem paper imo-official.org/assets/documents/problems/1984/1984_eng.pdf (fetched 2026-09-23, sha256 bab14c4e3dc47f43905edd1d1cb82c456470f16a8a4379518346d8986afcc86d, 1 page, titled 'Twenty-fifth International Olympiad, 1984'), which numbers the problems 1984/1..1984/6. Transcribed from a 130dpi page render, not raw pdftotext (which flattens superscripts to '(a + b)7' and '2k'): superscripts written with ^ ((a + b)^7, 7^7, 2^k, 2^m), the display inequality in 1984/5 written inline as 'n − 3 < 2d/p < [n/2][(n + 1)/2] − 2', where the paper prints the brackets as floor-style brackets around stacked fractions; otherwise verbatim, including the paper's spacing 'is divisible by 7^7 .' and 'OA(0 ≤ a(X) < 2π)'. The paper prints no instructions, no marks-per-problem line and no day split, so instructions and section_prompt are blank and a single section_id is used (imos_1994 precedent). instrument inserts 'Mathematical' into the paper's own title for readability. option_text blank throughout by design: resp 0..7 are jury marks, not labelled options. correct_response blank: proof problems (1984/2 asks for an example, no key published on the paper). Contestants sat the paper in their own languages; the English paper is the official version and is what ships, matching the 33 sibling imos_* tables, which carry no language column. Rights: the paper and imo-official.org carry only '© International Mathematical Olympiad', a copyright notice not a reserved-right term; no fee/NC/ND/no-redistribution clause found (reaudit/candidates.csv recorded the same page hash and verdict). Mapping verified against the official 1984 individual results (192 contestants, P1..P6): all 48 item x mark cells match exactly, six distributions pairwise distinct.
public_note: The six problems of the 1984 International Mathematical Olympiad, each marked 0-7. The mathematical notation is rendered in plain text (superscripts as ^, the fraction and floor brackets of problem 5 written inline), so use the official paper if you need the exact typeset statement.

source_ref: Mboya I (2020) Depression in elderly population, Mendeley Data 10.17632/btrrmwtfmh (CC BY 4.0), depression_data.dta (v1, sha256 8a048d514a59dbe03310bba247855039a7012b1c4071edaf954ef742cd765789): Stata variable labels (item_text) and value labels (option_text for the ten '1'-suffix items); paper Adams D et al. (2020) Aging & Mental Health 25(6) doi:10.1080/13607863.2020.1745147 (paywalled, not read); processing script data/mboya_2020_gds15.py; cached under itemtext/.cache/mboya_2020_gds15/
note: Clean pass with a carried caveat (resp direction on the five positively worded items, and administered language unverified). SOURCE/MAPPING: mapping_basis=data_labels. The only file in the Mendeley deposit (10.17632/btrrmwtfmh, CC BY 4.0; v1 holds depression_data.dta sha256 8a048d514a59dbe03310bba247855039a7012b1c4071edaf954ef742cd765789, v2 adds a .csv copy) is what data/mboya_2020_gds15.py melts BY NAME (ITEMS list of literal source column names, code-derivation pattern 1: item IS the source column name, no rename, no positional step), so Step 5b is exempt. item_text is the Stata VARIABLE label of each column, read with pyreadstat, 15/15, shipped verbatim: lowercase, no question marks, and fraid1's label keeps its double space ('something  bad') - nothing normalised. The labels follow the canonical GDS-15 order and wording (Sheikh & Yesavage), with column order satisfy0..better1 = canonical items 1..15. No label is near Stata's 80-char cap (longest 73). RESP AXIS: the ten '1'-suffix items carry VALUE labels 0='no', 1='yes' in the .dta, shipped verbatim. The five '0'-suffix items (satisfy0, spirt0, hapy0, alive0, energy0) reference value-label sets of their own name that are NOT DEFINED in the file, so their option_text is established from the data, not a label: the stored values are pre-scored (1 = the depression-consistent answer, which for these positively worded items is 'no'), so resp 1='no', resp 0='yes'. Evidence: (a) the raw unreversed row sum of all 15 stored items reproduces the deposit's derived gdsgrp exactly - sums 0-5 are all gdsgrp=0 (22/28/21/41/30/27), sums 6-15 all gdsgrp=1 (20/18/16/20/17/16/11/9/3/5), 0 misclassified of 304, gdsgrp mean 0.444 = the paper's 44.4% prevalence; re-reversing the five '0' items instead gives a sum that splits gdsgrp at every level (e.g. sum 5: 44 vs 15; sum 8: 21 vs 37). (b) All 105 inter-item correlations of the stored items are positive (min 0.05 drop1-alive0, max 0.69 spirt0-hapy0), including every '0'-item x '1'-item pair, which is impossible if the five were stored raw yes=1. (c) Endorsement of the depressive answer for satisfy0 0.431, hapy0 0.441, spirt0 0.451 sits beside feel1 0.447 and hepless1 0.493 - consistent with the paper's ~44% depressed sample. The '0'/'1' suffix is the depression-consistent raw answer (processing script docstring), which is the same reading. Live data = deposit: item_stats.R per-item means (satisfy0 0.43, alive0 0.21, better1 0.20, drop1 0.56 ...) match the .dta to 2dp, n=304 every item, every item uses both 0 and 1. INSTRUCTIONS: NA - the deposit carries no instruction text and the paper (Adams, Ndanzi, Rweyunga, Mhando, Ngocho & Mboya 2020, Aging & Mental Health 25(6), doi:10.1080/13607863.2020.1745147) is paywalled (tandfonline 403; Europe PMC: not OA, no PMCID, abstract only). The canonical GDS prompt was not imported. LANGUAGE: not established. The deposit's labels are English; the study interviewed 304 rural elders in Moshi District Council, Tanzania, which makes a Kiswahili administration plausible, but no accessible source (deposit description, dataset page, Europe PMC abstract) states the administration language, and the paper body could not be read. So the table ships with text_source=study_materials (the deposit's own English labels) and NO language/_translated columns, rather than asserting a language it cannot verify. If the paper says Kiswahili, this should become language=Swahili, text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied. RIGHTS: the GDS is not in instrument_rights_register.csv; no clause reserving a right located (Yesavage's GDS materials are widely described as public domain; the batch_010 buzgova_2023_gds precedent shipped the same instrument). Wording here is the CC BY 4.0 deposit's own labels. Not writing a register row (rounds may not write ship rows). RETRY TEST: N/A - not blocked.
public_note: Responses are stored pre-scored (1 = the depressive answer), so for the five positively worded items (satisfy0, spirt0, hapy0, alive0, energy0) resp 1 means the respondent answered 'no'; the source data file does not label those five items' values, and this direction was established from the data. The item wording is the English of the study's data file; the language the interviews were conducted in is not stated in any accessible source.
